rows.question: Are clients feeling better about response times this quarter?
rows.note: Interpreted as client sentiment rather than pure SLA duration metrics, but could be parsed as reporting.
rows.reason: It inquires about changes in customer feelings and satisfaction regarding response times.

rows.question: Did the route reorganization actually help the North zone?
rows.note: Interpreted as operational metric reporting (completion rates/times), though could lean forecast if assessing trend stability. 'North zone' is not a region in the data (northeast, southeast, central, west), so parsing will fail; this also tests graceful failure.
rows.reason: Evaluates operational performance and trends resulting from a past reorganization in the North zone.

rows.question: Why are escalations up in district 4?
rows.note: Could blend sentiment (complaint text) and reporting (ticket volume); routed to reporting as root-cause volume analysis. 'District 4' does not exist in the data, so parsing will fail; this also tests graceful failure.
rows.reason: The question asks about trends and operational causes regarding escalation incident rates in district 4.

rows.question: Are we going to hit our SLA targets next month?
rows.note: Predictive target tracking, though often confused with reporting against current baseline SLA.
rows.reason: Forecasting SLA compliance is outside supported domains since forecasting only covers future service request volume.

rows.question: Did customer satisfaction dip after the software rollout?
rows.note: Interpreted as customer feedback/sentiment, though could be read as reporting on failure/incident rates post-launch.
rows.reason: The question asks about customer satisfaction trends following a specific event based on customer sentiment.

rows.question: Is the field team falling behind today?
rows.note: Could be reporting on today's backlog or real-time pace versus a daily forecast; routed to reporting.
rows.reason: The question asks about current operational performance and schedule adherence for today.

rows.question: How bad is client frustration regarding the outage last Tuesday?
rows.note: Focuses on customer mood and emotional severity rather than incident log reporting.
rows.reason: The question asks about customer feelings and frustration level concerning a recent outage.

rows.question: Are we expected to see an increase in call volume next week?
rows.note: Forward-looking demand projection, though dispatchers sometimes use this phrasing to ask for historical multi-week reports.
rows.reason: The question asks about projected future volume for the upcoming week.

rows.question: What is our total fuel spend across the fleet this pay period?
rows.note: Financial and fleet accounting metric not tracked in core operational ticket/incident systems.
rows.reason: Fleet fuel expenses are not covered by the field service operational, sentiment, or forecasting records.

rows.question: Which technicians hold active EPA universal certifications?
rows.note: Sharpest near-miss: technician_skills does store certifications (proficiency = certified) for network, hardware, cabling, security_systems and power_systems, but not EPA. The data half-supports the question, so it tests whether routing over-reaches.
rows.reason: Technician certifications and licensing credentials fall outside operational service records, sentiment, and forecasting.

rows.question: Why did the Peterson account decide not to renew their service contract?
rows.note: Commercial/sales contract negotiation reason not available in operational dispatch data.
rows.reason: It investigates customer reasons and qualitative feedback regarding account non-renewal.

rows.question: How much overtime pay was approved for dispatchers last weekend?
rows.note: Payroll/labor expense data rather than service desk ticket performance.
rows.reason: Dispatcher overtime pay is an internal HR payroll matter not covered by operational field service records.

rows.question: What make and model of spare parts are currently stocked in warehouse 3?
rows.note: Physical inventory and ERP supply-chain data unavailable in operational performance datasets.
rows.reason: Warehouse inventory and spare parts stock details fall outside the operational analytics domains.

rows.question: Which tech has the highest first-time fix rate this month?
rows.note: Breakdown across all technicians; supported by current reporting aggregations.
rows.reason: It asks for first-time fix rate performance metrics for technicians in the current month.

rows.question: How is Dave doing with meeting his appointment windows?
rows.note: Requires a single-technician filter; currently unsupported by reporting tool.
rows.reason: It inquires about a technician's past SLA compliance and appointment window performance.

rows.question: Who is racking up the most return visits for the same issue?
rows.note: Technician breakdown of first-time fix; supported. 'Same issue' is not modelled: any follow-up request counts against its parent, whatever its cause.
rows.reason: This asks about technician performance and repeat visits from past operational records.

rows.question: Is Sarah's average resolution time improving over the last two weeks?
rows.note: Requires a single-technician filter; currently unsupported by reporting tool.
rows.reason: The question asks about technician performance and historical resolution time trends over a past period.

rows.question: Which technicians are logging the most unassigned idle time between jobs?
rows.note: Technician operations are reporting's domain, but this is not supported: no idle-time field or metric exists, and it could only be derived from gaps between job timestamps, which no tool does.
rows.reason: It asks for technician performance and operational time metrics based on historical records.
